datos.orejas: Oreja en botón (plegada), pequeña, de inserción alta y caída hacia delante
datos.recomendaciones_higiene: cepillado regular para mantener el pelaje en buen estado y prevenir nudos. limpieza de oidos si es necesario.
datos.alimentacion_recomendada: dieta balanceada de alta calidad, apropiada para su nivel de actividad.
datos.recomendaciones_alimentacion: controlar las porciones para evitar el sobrepeso. adaptar la dieta a la edad y nivel de actividad.
datos.recomendaciones_ejercicio_diario: Paseos diarios, juegos interactivos y oportunidades para correr en un área segura.
datos.advertencias_sobreesfuerzo: Evitar el ejercicio excesivo en climas muy calurosos.
datos.entorno_ideal: Rural o suburbano con espacio exterior.
datos.recomendaciones_adaptacion: Requiere un dueño experimentado que pueda manejar su energía y temperamento protector.
datos.cuidados_emocionales_recomendados: Requiere interacción social y sentirse parte de la familia.
datos.recomendaciones_generales_bienestar: Ofrecer un entorno seguro y estimulante, con oportunidades para socializar y ejercitarse.
datos.uso_original: Perro de granja, perro guardián y de compañía. Utilizado para cazar alimañas y proteger la propiedad.
datos.uso_actual: Principalmente perro de compañía y guardián familiar. Conserva su instinto de vigilancia.
datos.uso_en_trabajos: Vigilancia y compañía, ocasionalmente en deportes caninos.
datos.riesgos_craneo: Riesgos moderados: otitis, problemas dentales y riesgos propios de cada raza.

estandar.texto: FEDERATION CYNOLOGIQUE INTERNATIONALE (AISBL) SECRETARIAT GENERAL: 13, Place Albert 1er B – 6530 Thuin (Belgique) ______________________________________________________________________________ _______________________________________________________________ _______________________________________________________________ 05.05.2003/EN FCI-Standard N° 64 STERREICHISCHER PINSCHER (Austrian Pinscher) 2 TRANSLATION: Elke Peper. Official language (DE). ORIGIN: Austria. DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE OFFICIAL VALID STANDARD: 25.03.2003. UTILIZATION: Watch- and companion dog. FCI-CLASSIFICATION: Group 2 Pinscher and SchnauzerMolossoid breeds- Swiss Mountainand Cattle Dogs. Section 1.1 Pinscher. Without working trial. BRIEF HISTORICAL SUMMARY: The Austrian Pinscher descends from the ancient Austrian country pinschers that were widespread still in the second half of the 19th century, being modest, versatile farm dogs. In 1921 the systematic pure breeding of this breed began. On Oct. 16th, 1928, the breed was recognized by the Austrian Kennel Club (sterreichischer Kynologenverband) as sterreichischer kurzhaariger Pinscher (Austrian Shorthaired Pinscher). In the year 2000 the breed was renamed sterreichischer Pinscher (Austrian Pinscher). GENERAL APPEARANCE: Stocky dog of medium size with lively and bright expression. IMPORTANT PROPORTIONS: • The ratio of height at withers to length of body is 9 to 10. • The ratio of length of muzzle to length of skull is 4 to 6. 3 BEHAVIOUR / CHARACTER: Assertive, lively, alert, playful and especially devoted and friendly dealing with people familiar to him. Towards strangers he is suspicious and an incorruptible guard. His hunting instinct is only slightly developed. HEAD: Pear-shaped; in harmonious proportion to the body. CRANIAL REGION: Broad and rounded with pronounced frontal furrow and groove. Skull: Distinctly developed zygomatic arches, strong masticatory muscles. Stop: Well marked. FACIAL REGION: Nose: Black. Muzzle: Strong, nasal bridge straight. Lips: Tight, smooth, well fitting, with dark pigmentation. Jaws/Teeth: Strong, complete scissor bite. EYES: Large eyeball in round palpebral aperture, eyerims closefitting with dark pigmentation. EARS: Button ear (folded ear), small, set on high. NECK: Strong, of medium length. BODY: Withers: Well defined. Back: Short, broad, straight, tight. Loin: Short and broad. Croup: Long and broad. Chest: Long, deep, broad, barrel-shaped; well developed forechest. The muscles of the chest are strong and tight. Underline and belly: Slightly tucked up. TAIL: High set, strong, of medium length and densely covered with hair. 4 LIMBS: Strong bone. FOREQUARTERS: General appearance: Well muscled, straight legs, broad front. Shoulders: Shoulder blade long, well laid-back. Upper arm: Obliquely set. Forearm: Of medium length, straight. Carpal joint: Strong. Pastern: Short, moderately sloping. Forefeet: Close-knit with strong nails. HINDQUARTERS: General appearance: Well angulated. Upper thigh: Broad. Lower thigh: Of medium length. Hock joint: Strong. Metatarsus: Short. Hind feet: Close-knit with strong nails. GAIT / MOVEMENT: Flowing and harmonious movement covering a lot of ground. SKIN: Tight fitting. COAT: Hair: Thick double coat. The outer coat is short to medium-long, thick, smooth and close-lying. The undercoat is thick and short, buttocks slightly trousered. Colour: Russet gold (semmelgelb), brownish yellow, stag-red, black with tan-coloured markings. White markings: chest patch, muzzle, neck, throat, nape, feet and tip of tail. Lack of white markings is not a fault. SIZE: Height at the withers: 42 – 50 cm. (Males: 44 – 50 cm), (Bitches: 42 – 48 cm). 5 FAULTS: Any departure from the foregoing points should be considered a fault and the seriousness with which the fault should be regarded should be in exact proportion to its degree and its effect upon the health and welfare of the dog. DISQUALIFYING FAULTS: • Aggressive or overly shy. • Any dog clearly showing physical or behavioural abnormalities. • Undershot, overshot. N.B.: • Male animals should have two apparently normal testicles fully descended into the scrotum. • Only functionally and clinically healthy dogs, with breed typical conformation should be used for breeding.
